title: Number of 1 Bits
statement: Return how many bits are set in the binary representation of n, treating it as a 32-bit pattern.
hints: Test the lowest bit with n & 1, then shift right. Use an unsigned shift or a uint if you ever handle negatives.
That loops 32 times regardless of how many bits are set.
The trick n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit, so looping until n is zero runs once per set bit.
